text:
anna: FYI canary showing a noticeable perf regression after the platform stack bump (PR #2534). Small-sequence 95p latencies up ~35-45%. Blocking rollout until root cause known.

josh: numbers? which test/model/route?

anna: small-seq perf harness (gpt-smallish, seq=32-64) on dedicated pools. Before: 95p ~85ms. After: 95p ~118ms. Mean +~22ms. Traces attached to perf-ci job.

perf-ci-bot: perf/job/serve-small-seq: regression detected (95p +38%), compare commit a1b2c3 -> d4e5f6. https://ci.redwood/p/serve-small-seq/867

priya: did a nsight/nvprof run on a failing replica. Summary:

``nKernel attribution (per token):
- triton_gemm_fwd_v2           18.2%  (was 12.6% before)
- triton_gemm_fwd_generic      32.7%  (was 10.3% before)
- kv_cache_read                9.1%   (was 6.8%)
- attention_softmax            7.4%   (unchanged)
- dispatch/overhead            12.3%  (was 9.0%)
```

Big delta: generic GEMM use jumped and dispatch overhead increased. Also observed extra heap/workspace allocations for short sequences.

mike: which packages landed in #2534? I have PyTorch 1.14.0+cu12.3, cuDNN 8.8.1, and Triton 2.0.1 in the changelist.

priya: hypothesis: cuDNN/torch combo changed reported workspace/flop heuristics so Triton selector falls back to generic kernel for small M/K dims on this driver combo. That increases per-call overhead on short sequences.

josh: could KV cache layout or copy path changes explain memcpy spikes?

anna: nvtx shows an allocate+memcpy spike at first token for some calls — small but compounding across microbatches.

priya: single-request timeline (seq=48) from profiler:

``n0.0  enqueue
0.9  kv_cache_lookup + memcpy  (2.1ms)
5.2  GEMM_generic              (7.8ms)
12.0 GEMM_v2                  (4.1ms)
16.3 softmax                  (1.2ms)
18.0 token emit
```

Before the bump GEMM_generic was ~2.3ms and GEMM_v2 ~5.6ms (so kernel choice flipped).

anna: I'll kick a focused bisect over the bump set (torch/cudnn/titon combos). Can someone run an easy bisect?

bisect-bot: queued bisect job: range d4e5f6..d4e5f6~10 (includes torch, cudnn, triton). ETA ~45m.

~20m later...

bisect-bot: bisect result: regression traced to cuDNN 8.8.1 (as packaged for PyTorch 1.14 builds). Triton-only delta did not reproduce standalone.

priya: confirmed locally: forcing older cuDNN heuristic (export CUDNN_ALGO_SEARCH=HEURISTIC_PRE_8) restores previous kernel selection and recovers 95p to ~88ms. Not a long-term solution but a viable mitigation.

mike: can we gate that env override into canary for the small-seq route only? We should avoid changing behavior for long sequences until we understand perf tradeoffs.

josh: opened PR #2538 to set CUDNN_ALGO_SEARCH=HEURISTIC_PRE_8 scoped to the small-seq service route behind a feature flag. Added telemetry for long-seq tails.

deploy-bot: PR #2538 deployed to canary-small-route. 30m in: 95p back to ~90-95ms. No immediate long-seq regressions in initial checks.

priya: filing bug with cuDNN/PyTorch teams with reproducer and kernel timelines. Also proposing a CI microbenchmark that asserts stable kernel selection for short sequences to avoid silent shifts.

anna: action items: priya -> cuDNN bug report + reproducer (ETA 1d); mike -> vet env gating & rollout playbook (ETA today); josh -> keep PR #2538 in staging until upstream fix (monitor 24h).

sam: ops note: if we roll back globally, prepare a customer-facing blurb and check dedicated tenant overrides.

anna: thanks all, assigning rollout hold to eng-runtime until we have upstream plan. Closing thread once follow-ups posted.
